chunk_findings.detail:
`_misplaced` only reaches the new `wrong_tree_refusal(...)` call when `closed_item_refusal(...)` returned an *empty* `why` **and** an empty `_note`:

```python
why, _note = ( ... closed_item_refusal(it, force=force, reason=reason, ...) )
if not why and _note == "" and not (branch or commit):
    why = wrong_tree_refusal(repo, _load(repo, agent)[2], it, called_from)
```

`closed_item_refusal` is the helper that waives the "do not record on a COMPLETE item" rule when `--force` is given; in the waived case it does not refuse (`why == ""`) but returns a non-empty note recording the override. So the `_note == ""` term is false exactly on the documented override path, and the wrong-tree check is skipped. Concrete input: item `B` is COMPLETE; the caller's cwd is item `A`'s worktree; run `ddflow review B --gate rubber_duck --force`. `closed_item_refusal` yields `("", <force note>)`, `not why and _note == ""` is false, `wrong_tree_refusal` is never consulted, the review diffs item `A`'s tree, and a `rubber_duck` gate is recorded against `B` from the wrong diff — i.e. exactly the stray-gate scenario of B8b2dafcbf3, merely behind `--force`. The `--force` flag is scoped by the intent to the COMPLETE-item refusal ("refuses to record on a COMPLETE item without `--force`"); it should not also disable the wrong-tree guard, which is the primary fix here. Any state in which `closed_item_refusal` returns note-without-refusal makes the wrong-tree branch dead for that call, so the new guard is not unconditional.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_misplaced` short-circuits the completed-item rule whenever `commit` is truthy:

```python
why, _note = (
    ("", "")
    if commit
    else closed_item_refusal(it, force=force, reason=reason, what=f"reviewing {gate}")
)
if not why and not (branch or commit):
    why = wrong_tree_refusal(repo, _load(repo, agent)[2], it, called_from)
```

With `commit` set, `closed_item_refusal` is never consulted and `wrong_tree_refusal` is skipped, so `_misplaced` returns `None` and the review proceeds to record a gate — even when the target item is COMPLETE and no `--force` was given. The diff's own comment ("`--commit` is the after-merge review: recorded against the item, done or not") shows this is deliberate, but the stated intent of the fix is the opposite: "every gate verb refuses to record on a COMPLETE item without `--force`", and the regression test only covers the no-`--commit` path.

Concrete failure: `ddflow review B-hy-commit-events --commit <sha> --gate rubber_duck` run with no `--force`, once `B-hy-commit-events` is COMPLETE. `commit` is truthy, so `why` stays `""`, the wrong-tree guard is also skipped, `_misplaced` returns `None`, and a stray `rubber_duck` event is appended to a completed item's log — exactly the harm (a stray gate event on the already-completed `B-hy-commit-events`) that bug B8b2dafcbf3 was filed for. Either `closed_item_refusal` must also be applied on the `--commit` path (gated on `not force`), or the exception needs to be explicit and tested rather than contradicting the stated rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_misplaced (the `commit` short-circuit)

chunk_findings.detail: The `--force` half of this regression test does not exercise the code path that the earlier review's finding was about, so it does not actually guard that regression. Item `A` is only *claimed* at line 83 (`run_cli(repo, "claim", "A")`); it is never made complete. For an in-progress item, `closed_item_refusal(...)` returns an empty `why` **and** an empty `_note` regardless of `--force`, so the guard `if not why and _note == "" and not (branch or commit):` (the line the prior finding flagged) evaluates the same way with or without the fix, and `wrong_tree_refusal(...)` is reached either way. The previous defect only manifests when the item *is* COMPLETE and `--force` is passed (that is when `closed_item_refusal` waives the rule and yields a non-empty `_note` while leaving `why` empty, which is exactly what previously made `wrong_tree_refusal` unreachable). Because `A` here is open, this test passes against the buggy `_note == ""` version too, i.e. it would not have failed on the pre-fix code. Likewise, no test in this file covers the actual reported incident — a review of a *completed* item run from another item's tree. To guard the previous finding, this case needs an item that is finished (e.g. finish `A` before running `_from(repo, tree_b, "review", "A", ..., "--force", ...)`); as written the `--force` assertion is vacuous for that path.

chunk_findings.detail: The completed-item guard is skipped entirely whenever `commit` is truthy, so the very class of event B8b2dafcbf3 is about can still be written. Concretely: with item `B-hy-commit-events` in state COMPLETE, running `ddflow review B-hy-commit-events --gate rubber_duck --commit <ref>` takes the `commit` arm, `why` stays `""`, the `not (branch or commit)` guard also suppresses the wrong-tree check, and the review proceeds and records a gate event against the finished item with no `--force`. That is exactly the symptom described in the bug (status still shows passed, but a stray gate event is in the log), and it contradicts the stated fix that "every gate verb refuses to record on a COMPLETE item without --force" — the commit form is the input that demonstrates the guard is not applied. If the after-merge review genuinely must be recorded on a finished item, the guard should still run (so `--force` is demanded and the operator's intent is explicit) rather than being bypassed.

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement assertion `assert "state done" in run_cli(repo, "show", "P1.T1")[1]` no longer exercises the behavior this bug fix is about. The removed `_finish(repo, "P1.T1")` call was the only visible gate verb invocation on the parent after it became COMPLETE via its last child. The stated fix requires gate verbs to refuse recording on a COMPLETE item without `--force`; with that call gone, the test would still pass even if `_finish` wrongly recorded a stray gate. The substring check is also weak: `show P1.T1` prints the subtree, so “state done” can come from the already-completed child `P1.T1a` even if the parent never auto-closed. The test should assert the parent’s own state/refusal directly, e.g. `_finish(repo, "P1.T1")[0] == REFUSED`.
